Projects you own are not deleted automatically; the administrator can give them a new owner.

ptg1.readme.text: The cut is at the midpoint of the overlap, rounded along the film. Shot lengths are differences between rounded boundaries. handleIn and handleOut are overlap on the neighbour’s side; shoot including the handles. Without overlap, handles are 0. Audio and words belong to the shot where the event starts, retain their full length and include absolute and relative times; crossesCut=true marks a crossing. Twos are 12 exposures/s on a 24 fps timeline, every other frame. Out timecode and Frame Out are exclusive. An empty film has 0 frames; a scene shorter than one capture frame may have 0 frames and remains listed. The camera field is built from the scene's rig (B-087) with one sample per exposure; it is null when the shot lacks a 2D composition or a usable rig.

ptg3.readme-camera.text: This package contains one FBX file (ASCII 7.4) per shot with the camera move in physical units: time in KTime (46,186,158,000 per second), FilmWidth in inches, FocalLength in mm, and the plates as null objects. The FBX export is experimental – try it on your rig and report any discrepancies.

ptg3.readme-ae.text: Open After Effects, choose File > Scripts > Run Script File and run bygg.jsx from this folder. The script builds one composition per shot and a main composition with layers, keyframes, image swaps, masks and audio. Transitions between scenes are not included. Text layers are not recreated.

ptg3.readme-modes.text: Camera modes: "AE camera (3D)" creates a 3D camera in After Effects with the focal length and sensor from the rig. "2D parallax" creates no camera; instead each plate gets a null object (PAR_) that moves and scales its layers according to the plate's parallax. The FBX files always contain the 3D camera. The camera has one key per exposure at the capture frame rate (every other frame on twos).

ptg3.readme-fbx-binary.text: The files are ASCII FBX. Many programs, Blender among them, only read binary FBX; convert the file first, for example with Autodesk FBX Converter or Assimp. The FBX export is experimental until it has been tried in Dragonframe or another production program.

The shot composition itself and the main composition are unchanged. Render <shot>_RENDER and import the film with the QR code; the title card is trimmed off on import.

ptg2.readme.text: Dragonframe package: one folder per shot, named as in the shot list. Each folder has a reference film (_ref.mp4, H.264) at the capture frame rate, frame-accurate and including the handles; on twos each exposure is shown for two frames. The optional PNG sequence (png/) has one file per exposure, numbered like the X-sheet rows; the reference film keeps every frame. Audio (audio/) is WAV 48 kHz 24-bit, as long as the shot including handles, with volume points and fades baked in: one stem per character (DIA_), ambience (AMB), music (MUS), effects (SFX) and a full mix (MIX), in the selected language version. The X-sheet is provided as CSV and PDF (A4 and Letter), with one row per exposure; the mouth column stays empty until mouth names are added. Importing into Dragonframe: 1) Open the scene, choose Video Assist / reference layer and import _ref.mp4 (or the PNG sequence) as reference. 2) Import the MIX file, or the dialogue stem, in the Audio window and set its start to frame 1. 3) Open the X-Sheet and import xsheet.csv, or print the PDF next to the rig. AI can be used for track reading of the dialogue, but the package is made entirely without AI.

ptg7.readme.text: Nuke and Fusion: extract the entire ZIP and open the shot's .nk or .comp. Media paths are relative to the shot folder. Set the working directory to the shot folder if the application does not resolve relative paths. World units are millimetres, Y up, camera facing negative Z. Card2 is Nuke's classic 3D card (Card), not the 2D projection node Card3D. Camera field of view and position follow the model per frame; twos are held. Fusion uses ImagePlane3D. No AI is used. Real import must be checked in Nuke and Fusion before production.

ptg7.no-rig.text: {shot}: no valid rig; 2D setup with Transform nodes, without a 3D camera.

ptg6.readme.text: Editorial files: import OTIO, FCP7-XML (xmeml v5) or CMX 3600 EDL. Paths are relative to the package. Timecode is non-drop-frame. Twos retain 24 fps. Reference films include handles; transitions are applied in the editor, not baked into reference films. Audio is a per-shot mix with volume keys and fades baked in; no extra audio transition. The active take is used, otherwise the animatic. Wipe/push/iris are described in metadata, but the standard editorial transition is a cross dissolve. No AI is used.

ptg6.media-included.text: Media files are included. Extract the entire package before import.

ptg6.media-linked.text: Media files are not included. Place reference films and MIX audio at the listed relative paths, or relink them in your editor.

ptg4.readme.text: Mouth list: PDF and CSV show exposures per character and mouth. JSON uses zero-based frames, including handles. Moho DAT uses Papagayo mouths and one-based frames at capture fps; twos repeat. Outdated tracks are exported unchanged and marked in JSON. NB Uttale (CC0) and CMUdict (BSD) run locally. No AI or paid calls.
